title: pmx actions v2
description: What an agent returns for one bar: a probability for every open market it addresses, at most one order intent per market, an optional research request, notes, lessons (LLM only) and a rationale that goes to the trace and never to the journal. This exact file is handed to the Claude Code CLI through --json-schema, so it is flat and strict: every property of an item is required, with null for the ones that do not apply. Semantics (kind versus fields, market open, cash) live in the runner, CONTRACTS_V2 section 8.4. One item per market: a second item on the same market_id in one bar is action_rejected(duplicate) whatever its kind, and the first occurrence in submission order wins, including its prob_ppm. JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness on a property of an array item, so the runner enforces it.

target_position.description: Contracts on a binary, milli-units on a continuous instrument (CONTRACTS_V2 17.1, ruling R148); the runner enforces the per-kind bound.

price_bp.description: bp on a binary (1..9999, enforced by the runner), ticks on a continuous instrument.

horizon_forecasts.description: Amendment C1b (CONTRACTS_V2 17.5, rulings R157 and R184): one entry per (market_id, horizon_bars) of the run's horizons for the open continuous instruments; optional, a binary-only agent omits it. A missing pair is carried (the previous statement, else the random walk), except the shortest horizon of a market the agent addressed: when no pair states it, the runner synthesises it from that market's prob_ppm with quantiles_ticks null, so a family that sends only prob_ppm states a direction. A pair that is present for the shortest horizon must equal the market's prob_ppm, else action_rejected(bad_prob); a duplicate pair is action_rejected(duplicate) with the first occurrence winning; a horizon outside the config is bad_horizon; a quantile tuple that is not five non-decreasing prices is bad_quantiles.
